channel.description: Latest articles from Andalusia Star News (andalusiastarnews.com)

item.title: Mizell honors community and American Heart Month
item.description: Mizell Memorial Hospital marks American Heart Month in red, while its Auxiliary’s Valentine’s Tree lets residents honor loved ones and local leaders with heart ornaments.

item.title: APL honors Black History through weekly author features
item.description: Andalusia Public Library marks Black History Month with weekly spotlights on African American authors, from S.A. Cosby and Tracy Deonn to Amy DuBois Barnett and Kwame Alexander.

item.title: Lillian Connally Renfroe Obituary
item.description: Obituary: Lillian Connally Renfroe, devoted wife, mother and “Nana,” died at home Feb. 15. A memorial service will be held Feb. 21 at 11 a.m. at Trinity Presbyterian Church in Pensacola.

item.title: AG affirms Cozart’s murder conviction
item.description: Alabama appeals court upholds life sentence for Teddy Donnell Cozart in killing of Treyvous Cobbins, an essential witness in a separate murder case.

item.title: AHS FFA to compete at State Envirothon
item.description: Andalusia High School FFA is headed to its first-ever State Envirothon, with six students set to compete Feb. 26-28 at 4-H Camp in Columbiana after months of preparation.

item.title: AYWC Brings Home Regional and State Victories
item.description: AYWC wrestlers captured multiple regional and state titles, with young champions leading a push to grow the sport locally and bring wrestling into Covington County schools.

item.title: JavaTime expands to second location
item.description: Andalusia's JavaTime is opening a second shop at 1305 River Falls Street by early March, adding breakfast, lunch items and catering to better serve the other side of town.

item.title: CCS CINDERELLA SHINES
item.description: Covington County Schools Collaborative Arts staged a student-led production of Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella at Straughn High School, delivering professional work onstage and behind the scenes.

item.title: Jail Report from February 17 to February 18
item.description: Covington County Jail bookings for Feb. 17–18 detail arrests on drug, DUI, trespass, theft and failure-to-appear charges, with bonds ranging from $229 to $250,000.
